item.title: The Last Dry Seat

turns.text: Make a silent 15-second widescreen short in three scenes. A young woman with a curly black bob and yellow raincoat finds a wet park bench. An older man with a white beard and blue coat offers his folded newspaper to sit on. They sit together and smile. Live-action look, sweet rather than cheesy.

item.tests: Turns two described characters and a simple story into one assembled 15-second film with a readable setup, kind gesture and resolution.

answer_sheet.Characters: A young adult woman with a curly black bob and yellow raincoat; an older adult man with a white beard and blue coat.
answer_sheet.Story and setting: A wet park bench; the woman finds it wet, the man offers his folded newspaper as a dry seat, then they sit together and smile.
answer_sheet.Length and format: One 15-second widescreen 16:9 video, with three scenes.
answer_sheet.Sound, dialogue and text: Silent, with no dialogue, captions or titles.

must_haves: One playable 15-second widescreen film contains three sequential scenes, not separate clip deliverables.
The woman has a curly black bob and yellow raincoat; the man has a white beard and blue coat.
The opening visibly establishes that the park bench is wet.
The man offers a folded newspaper as a dry place to sit, and the ending shows both characters seated together and smiling.
The film has a live-action appearance and no audible soundtrack.
After the follow-up, the final result is vertical 9:16 (the user changed the shape from widescreen 16:9); everything else is as before.

style.prompt: Create a silent 15-second widescreen live-action short film in exactly three sequential scenes, approximately five seconds each, with clean straight cuts. Understated, observational, sweet but never cheesy. Realistic human movement, natural overcast daylight after rain, muted green park setting, delicate film grain, authentic cinematic photography. Maintain identical characters and wardrobe throughout: an adult young woman in her late twenties with a curly black bob haircut and a yellow raincoat; an older adult man with a white beard and a blue coat. One continuous simple story at the same wet wooden park bench. SCENE 1, 0–5 seconds: medium-wide eye-level shot. The woman approaches the park bench, notices rainwater glistening on the seat, lightly touches the wet slats and pauses, looking for a dry place to sit. The older man stands near the other end holding a folded newspaper. SCENE 2, 5–10 seconds: medium two-shot, gentle closer framing. The older man notices her hesitation and quietly offers his folded newspaper with a small friendly gesture. She accepts with a grateful restrained smile and lays the folded newspaper flat on the wet seat as a dry pad. Make the newspaper handoff clear, physically plausible, and unhurried. SCENE 3, 10–15 seconds: steady medium-wide two-shot. She sits on the folded newspaper, and he sits beside her with a comfortable respectful gap. They exchange a brief warm glance and small genuine smiles, then relax looking out into the park. Hold the final quiet moment. No romance signaling, no exaggerated grinning, no theatrical gestures, no sentimentality. No dialogue, no voiceover, no music, no sound, no subtitles, no titles, no logos. Preserve clear action continuity and the woman's black curly bob, yellow raincoat, man's white beard and blue coat across all three shots.
